design.estimator: pred + eb_offset + (b_post-1)*(pred - mean_cal(pred)); b_post shrinks the within-paper OLS slope toward 1 with tau_b2
design.tau_b2: between-paper slope variance, method of moments on training folds, papers with >=5 rows
design.oracles: in-sample per paper, three model classes, same rows as n_cal=0
design.amendment: 2026-10-23T05:40+08:00 no_collapse_n1 added before any run, because the existing UP-26 affine arm scores 0.4258 at n_cal=1

oracle.definition: per paper, in-sample: constant = mean residual; affine = OLS y~f; isotonic = monotone y~f. Same evaluation rows as n_cal=0.

kill.rule: affine oracle < 0.72 => the constant offset is the ceiling

caveats: All three oracles are in-sample per paper: they see every row of the paper they are scored on. They bound what a per-paper model class can do, not what a 10-row estimator can do.
The isotonic oracle has as many parameters as the paper has rows, so it is the loosest of the three and is reported for completeness only.
tau_b2 is estimated from papers with at least 5 training rows. Papers below that threshold get the pooled value, which is the same choice UP-26 makes for kappa.
The slope is clipped to [0, 2], matching UP-26's affine arm; without the clip two calibration rows with near-identical predictions produce an unbounded b.
n_cal<3 returns b_post=1, so the arm is exactly the EB arm there. The no_collapse check is therefore a statement about the estimator, not the slope.
